scope: Actual 16 cases, P/B/U/R/S renders, runner source and all 80 saved outputs; no GPU/network/new generation.
claims_input: Paraphrased new-user-claim summary supplied by parent agent; not a verbatim user quotation.

claim_audits.claim: Full emits one integer because one token forward cannot compute multi-step arithmetic and therefore copies old answer
claim_audits.evidence: All eight E Full outputs are bare integers plus punctuation, but only E01/E03/E06/E07 equal the old terminal value; E05 is correct. Decode uses multiple token forwards, and output length is not hidden arithmetic depth.

claim_audits.claim: E02 late's 28 in 28*2=56 is an old intermediate value left in U
claim_audits.evidence: U has no numbers; B has x24,y15,z30. R newly states x28. Equation matches applying outer z=2*y to the revised x as if it were y, skipping y=x-9; this is a compatible variable-binding/omitted-composition description, not established KV-source causality.

claim_audits.claim: Early rescues E02/E03/E05/E07 because lack of copyable result forces explicit re-derivation
claim_audits.evidence: Those early outputs contain correct substitutions, but the four are not four gains over Full: E05 Full is already correct (28), Late harms it (34), Early restores it (28). E07 Late and Early already give the identical correct equation (37). Only E02/E03 are Early repairs of both Full and Late. Output format was not randomized; fresh state, attention and generated form change together.

claim_audits.claim: E01/C04 failures prove whole-B deletion removed independent y/z evidence
claim_audits.evidence: All cases have x->y->z. E01 old y38/z33 descend from wrong x12; C04 values are valid descendants of correct x17. In both, P retains every definition. 11-5/17-9 omit the y transformation, but do not identify removal of independent y/z.

claim_audits.claim: After deleting B in W, R is the only evidence left; trusting latest revision must fail by theorem
claim_audits.evidence: P and all definitions remain readable in all arms. Only one of eight target W outputs equals the full result implied by the wrong revision; several instead omit a transformation. A conditional statement assuming wrong revision and unquestioning use is not a new explanation of these outputs.

claim_audits.claim: Same 16 cases can compare whole-B against closed FaultOnly retaining independent y/z and strictly prove half of failures are deletion of independent support
claim_audits.evidence: Closure of disputed x is x,y,z and leaves no B_shared in 16/16. Root+direct child deletes x,y but retains stale descendant z. Closed FaultOnly and whole-B have the same asserted content; differences from delimiter/operator tokens would be a different hypothesis. No predeclared result can strictly prove a fixed half attribution.

suggested_minimal_new_graph.shared_visible_revision: Wait, x should be 28; recompute its consequences from the original definitions.
suggested_minimal_new_graph.recommended_serialization: P | B_shared(r=9) | B_bad(x=24,y=15,u=30,z=39) | U | R | S
suggested_minimal_new_graph.reason: Retaining r is actually independent of the disputed x. Place shared r before the bad branch to prevent its cached state from already reading that branch. Its original definition remains visible in P for every arm; this tests reuse of valid work, not withholding the task specification.
suggested_minimal_new_graph.if_shared_is_after_bad_branch: Semantic independence alone does not make its KV independent. Recompute retained downstream r from the clean visible prefix before calling its state clean.

design_recommendations: Do not GPU-run WholeB vs purported closed FaultOnly on the current 16-case x->y->z set; the proposed independent-support contrast is empty.

If testing output format, use a separate frozen 2x2 context(full vs whole-B early) x format(integer vs one-line substitution); no new correct y/z in instructions, record actual tokens, and do not call format-mediated gains proof of latent single-forward incapacity.
For an actual shared-support experiment add an independent root r and a final merge z=u+r; compute closure from known structural provenance, including the final z descendant.
Distinguish semantic dependency closure from dense-Transformer cache dependency: an r statement serialized after a faulty span may have a context-dependent cache despite arithmetic independence.

Hold visible revision/summary token IDs and original positions equal for late-vs-fresh comparisons. A correct new y or z summary is new privileged computation, not preservation of old independent work.
Separate closure-preservation, cache recomputation and output format rather than adding all factors and attributing one combined effect to independent evidence.
Use equal-count, age/contiguity-aware retention controls where possible; keeping r means retaining more valid tokens than deleting all, so mask budget alone does not resolve semantic specificity.
Keep no-error and false-Wait controls, and explicitly mark any oracle-triggered arm as an offline upper bound rather than an online detector.
